answer: Price the attack by its payoff, not the account. A verdict worth V settles only after each juror in the deciding quorum escrows coin equal to V, burned in full if a later audit overturns the ruling. Capturing that decision thus costs >=V of real at-risk capital every attempt, and a thousand cheap keys buy no discount: the bond tracks the prize, not the headcount. Sybils may creep wide as a vine or hit with the force of a gale, yet each clone still forfeits the whole stake, as a lotus shuts at dusk. Attacker cost: >=V per captured verdict, scaling with the reward, never the identity count.
